Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

OECDscaleup 0.2.0.9000 (development version)

The development version, on the default branch ScalerAnalysis.

  • One package for the routines that were separate before. The trade package (firm-level trade in goods: exporters, importers and exporting scalers) runs from the same package and the same configuration (run_trade_pipeline()).
  • New scaler analysis. The fastest-growing scalers (compute_top_scalers()) and scalers growing into mid-caps (compute_midcap_transitions()), run from files by run_scaler_analysis().
  • Documentation. The variable dictionary of the input data as a dataset (variable_dictionary) and two articles on the input variables; check_inputs() checks a country’s files before a run; a step-by-step walkthrough of the whole analysis on simulated data (example_scaleup_data()).
  • Performance. A panel of 8 million firm-years runs in about 15 minutes with under 20 GB of memory.
  • config_scaleup() now requires nace_revision, the NACE revision of the sector codes ("2" or "2.1").
  • Some indicator computations were revised, so results can differ from version 0.1.0.

OECDscaleup 0.1.0

The translation to R of the OECD Scale Up routines written in Stata (the “Second Package”, version 1.3): build_accounts_indicators(), compute_characteristics(), compute_persistence(), compute_contribution() and compute_predictors(), run from files by run_scaleup_pipeline(). The results were checked table by table against those of the original routines. This version is kept on the branch Stata-to-R.
